items.q: By the time Lan gets home from school, her little brother ______ all the birthday cake.
items.vi: Đến lúc Lan đi học về thì em trai cô ấy sẽ ăn hết cả cái bánh sinh nhật rồi.
items.explanation: By the time + present simple (gets home) marks a future point, and an action finished before that point takes the future perfect: will have eaten. ✗ has eaten — present perfect, links a past action to now, not to a future deadline; ✗ ate — past simple, but the cake-eating has not happened yet; ✗ is eating — present continuous, an action in progress now, not one completed before she arrives.

items.q: Could you ______ the kitchen floor? There are crumbs everywhere after the party.
items.vi: Bạn quét sàn bếp giúp mình được không? Sau bữa tiệc, vụn bánh rơi khắp nơi.
items.explanation: The clue is the kitchen floor and crumbs: you sweep a floor with a broom. ✗ dust — wipe dust off shelves or furniture, not crumbs off a floor; ✗ fold — bend clothes or paper neatly; ✗ hang — put clothes or pictures up on a line or wall.

items.q: Nam's parents ______ when they found out he had skipped school to go to a party.
items.vi: Bố mẹ Nam nổi giận đùng đùng khi phát hiện cậu ấy trốn học đi dự tiệc.
items.explanation: The clue is found out he had skipped school: parents react with anger, and go through the roof means to become extremely angry. ✗ went round in circles — made no progress; ✗ went down the drain — was wasted (money, effort); ✗ went off the rails — started behaving badly, which fits Nam, not his parents.

items.q: Lan: Shall I bring some snacks tonight? / Nam: No, you ______ — my mum has made enough for everyone.
items.vi: Lan: Tối nay mình mang chút đồ ăn vặt tới nhé? / Nam: Không, cậu không cần đâu — mẹ mình đã làm đủ cho mọi người rồi.
items.explanation: Needn't = it is not necessary, matching the reason my mum has made enough for everyone. ✗ mustn't — forbids ("you are not allowed to"), too strong for an offer of snacks; ✗ can't — denies ability or permission, not necessity; ✗ won't — a refusal or a prediction, not an answer to "Shall I?".

items.q: The letters on our badge, ______ stand for the school's name, were designed by a student.
items.vi: Các chữ cái trên huy hiệu của chúng tôi, vốn là viết tắt của tên trường, do một học sinh thiết kế.
items.explanation: The commas mark a non-defining clause about a thing (the letters), so which is needed. ✗ that — cannot introduce a non-defining clause after a comma; ✗ who — for people, not letters; ✗ whose — possessive, needs a noun after it (whose colours).

items.q: Minh is ______ a real effort to finish his homework before the party starts.
items.vi: Minh đang thực sự cố gắng làm xong bài tập về nhà trước khi bữa tiệc bắt đầu.
items.explanation: The fixed collocation is make an effort, and the object a real effort decides it. ✗ doing — we do homework or the dishes, not an effort; ✗ taking — we take a break or a photo; ✗ having — we have a party or a rest; none of these pair with effort.

items.q: It's your turn to ______ the dishes tonight; I did them yesterday.
items.vi: Tối nay đến lượt cậu rửa bát; hôm qua mình rửa rồi.
items.explanation: The object the dishes decides it: we wash the dishes (= wash up). ✗ mop — clean a floor with a wet mop; ✗ sweep — clean a floor with a broom; ✗ dust — wipe dust off furniture and shelves.

items.q: Hung only bought that expensive phone to ______ in front of his classmates.
items.vi: Hùng mua cái điện thoại đắt tiền đó chỉ để khoe khoang trước mặt các bạn cùng lớp.
items.explanation: The clue is expensive phone ... in front of his classmates: show off = try to impress people with what you have. ✗ show up — arrive, appear; ✗ put off — postpone, or make someone dislike something; ✗ take off — remove clothes, or leave the ground (a plane).

items.q: Lan: Where's Nam? / Hoa: He ______ his homework in the library — he'll be back at six.
items.vi: Lan: Nam đâu rồi? / Hoa: Cậu ấy đang làm bài tập trong thư viện — sáu giờ sẽ về.
items.explanation: Hoa is saying where Nam is at this moment (Where's Nam? ... he'll be back at six), so the present continuous is doing is needed. ✗ does — present simple, a habit or routine, not what is happening now; ✗ has done — present perfect, would mean the homework is finished; ✗ did — past simple, a finished past action, but he is still in the library.

items.q: Before the party, we had to ______ the living room so there was space to dance.
items.vi: Trước bữa tiệc, chúng tôi phải dọn gọn phòng khách để có chỗ nhảy.
items.explanation: The clue is so there was space to dance: to tidy a room is to put things in order and clear space. ✗ mend — repair something broken; ✗ polish — rub shoes or furniture to make them shine; ✗ iron — press clothes flat with a hot iron.

items.q: I have very ______ homework tonight, so I can come to Hoa's party after all.
items.vi: Tối nay mình có rất ít bài tập, nên rốt cuộc mình có thể đến dự tiệc của Hoa.
items.explanation: Homework is uncountable, and the meaning (so I can come) is "almost none", so little fits; it is also the only option that can follow very. ✗ few — for plural countable nouns (few books); ✗ a few — countable, and "very a few" is impossible; ✗ a little — uncountable but positive ("some"), and very a little does not exist.

items.q: If I ______ more free time after school, I would join the school band.
items.vi: Nếu mình có nhiều thời gian rảnh sau giờ học hơn, mình sẽ tham gia ban nhạc của trường.
items.explanation: Would join in the main clause marks a second conditional (unreal present), so the if-clause takes the past simple: If I had. ✗ have — first conditional, would need will join; ✗ had had — past perfect belongs to the third conditional (would have joined); ✗ would have — would never goes in the if-clause.

items.q: Hurry up, or we will ______ the last bus home and have to call a taxi.
items.vi: Nhanh lên, không thì chúng ta sẽ lỡ chuyến xe buýt cuối cùng về nhà và phải gọi taxi đấy.
items.explanation: The clue is the last bus and have to call a taxi: you miss a bus, train or flight when you arrive too late for it. ✗ lose — be unable to find something, or be beaten in a game; ✗ fail — not pass a test or exam; ✗ drop — let something fall.

items.q: Dad ______ the bookshelves every weekend because the dust makes my brother sneeze.
items.vi: Cuối tuần nào bố cũng lau bụi giá sách vì bụi làm em trai tôi hắt hơi.
items.explanation: The clue is bookshelves and the dust: to dust is to wipe dust off furniture. ✗ rinses — washes with clean water to remove soap; ✗ peels — removes the skin of fruit or vegetables; ✗ stirs — mixes food or drink with a spoon.

items.q: Hoa ______ the party yet — her bag and jacket are still on the chair.
items.vi: Hoa không thể nào đã rời bữa tiệc được — túi và áo khoác của cô ấy vẫn còn trên ghế.
items.explanation: The evidence her bag and jacket are still on the chair calls for a negative deduction: can't have left = it is impossible that she left. ✗ must have left — the opposite deduction ("I'm sure she left"), which the evidence contradicts; ✗ should have left — she was expected to leave but didn't, a criticism, not a deduction; ✗ needn't have left — she did leave but it was unnecessary, which contradicts yet.

items.q: Studying a little every day feels hard now, but it will pay off ______.
options: on the spur of the moment
at the drop of a hat
items.vi: Mỗi ngày học một chút bây giờ thấy vất vả, nhưng về lâu dài sẽ có kết quả.
items.explanation: The contrast hard now ... will pay off points to a distant result: in the long run = over a long period, eventually. ✗ in the nick of time — just before it is too late; ✗ on the spur of the moment — suddenly, without planning; ✗ at the drop of a hat — immediately, without hesitation.

items.q: Mr Tran ______ maths at our school since 2015, and he still loves the job.
items.vi: Thầy Trần đã dạy toán ở trường chúng tôi từ năm 2015, và thầy vẫn yêu công việc này.
items.explanation: Since 2015 links a past starting point to now, and he still loves the job confirms it continues, so the present perfect has taught is needed. ✗ taught — past simple, a finished period, would mean he no longer teaches there; ✗ is teaching — present continuous cannot be used with since + a starting point; ✗ had taught — past perfect, needs a later past point to be "before".

items.q: The café ______ we usually meet at after school is closed for repairs this week.
items.vi: Quán cà phê mà bọn mình hay gặp nhau sau giờ học tuần này đóng cửa để sửa chữa.
items.explanation: The clause is defining (no commas) and keeps its preposition at the end (meet at), so a place-thing takes that (or which). ✗ where — already means "at which", so it cannot combine with at; ✗ whom — for people only; ✗ whose — possessive, needs a noun after it.

items.q: Everyone says Mai ______ her mother — they have the same laugh and the same smile.
items.vi: Ai cũng bảo Mai giống mẹ — hai mẹ con có cùng tiếng cười và nụ cười.
items.explanation: The clue is the same laugh and the same smile as her mother: take after = resemble an older relative. ✗ takes up — start a hobby or activity; ✗ looks after — care for someone; ✗ takes off — remove clothes, or leave the ground.

items.q: Hang the ______ on the line outside; it won't dry indoors in this weather.
items.vi: Phơi quần áo giặt lên dây ngoài trời đi; thời tiết này để trong nhà sẽ không khô đâu.
items.explanation: The clue is hang ... on the line and dry: laundry is washed clothes, which you hang out to dry. ✗ rubbish — waste, which you take out; ✗ dishes — plates and bowls, which you wash and dry with a cloth; ✗ groceries — food shopping, which you put away.

items.q: ______ the bad weather, the school football match went ahead on Sunday afternoon.
items.vi: Dù thời tiết xấu, trận bóng đá của trường vẫn diễn ra vào chiều Chủ nhật.
items.explanation: The blank is followed by a noun phrase (the bad weather), so it needs a preposition: Despite. ✗ Although — a conjunction, needs a clause with subject and verb (although the weather was bad); ✗ In spite — incomplete, must be in spite of; ✗ Even though — also a conjunction, needs a full clause.

items.q: Remember ______ the lights before you leave the classroom this afternoon.
items.vi: Nhớ tắt đèn trước khi rời lớp chiều nay nhé.
items.explanation: Remember + to-infinitive = don't forget to do something in the future, and before you leave shows the action is still to come: to turn off. ✗ turning off — remember + -ing is a memory of something already done, which makes no sense as a reminder; ✗ turn off — remember cannot take a bare infinitive; ✗ to turning off — to + -ing does not follow remember.

items.q: When I called at seven, my friends ______ for the party, so nobody answered the phone.
items.vi: Lúc mình gọi vào bảy giờ, các bạn mình đang chuẩn bị cho bữa tiệc, nên không ai nghe máy.
items.explanation: A longer action in progress when a shorter past action interrupted it (When I called at seven) takes the past continuous: were getting ready. ✗ got ready — past simple, a completed action, but they were in the middle of it, which is why nobody answered; ✗ have got ready — present perfect cannot combine with the past time at seven; ✗ are getting ready — present continuous, but the story is in the past.

items.q: We're ______ a party on Saturday to celebrate the end of the exams — can you come?
items.vi: Thứ Bảy này bọn mình tổ chức một bữa tiệc mừng thi xong — cậu đến được không?
items.explanation: The object a party decides it: we throw (or have / hold) a party. ✗ making — we make a cake or an effort, not a party; ✗ doing — we do homework or the dishes; ✗ taking — we take a break or a photo; none of these collocate with party.

items.q: ______ does Lan miss a homework deadline; she is the most organised student in the class.
items.vi: Hiếm khi Lan trễ hạn nộp bài tập; cô ấy là học sinh ngăn nắp nhất lớp.
items.explanation: The inverted verb does Lan miss shows a negative adverb starts the sentence, and the meaning (the most organised student) needs "almost never": Rarely. ✗ No sooner — needs a past perfect verb and than (no sooner had she ... than); ✗ Not until — needs a time phrase or clause before the inversion (not until Friday does she ...); ✗ Only after — also needs a time phrase or clause first (only after lunch does she ...).
